parsed.explanation: The combined regime lacks a general criminal ban on trans identity, and the division has no statewide adult bathroom ban. But the national layer creates traveller-facing exposure: sex-marker passport restrictions, entry screening that can refuse cases and consider lifetime fraud ineligibility, federal facility exclusion, and documented harm in immigration and corrections custody. The division adds a school-only facility ban, a minors' care ban, a hate-crime statute omitting gender identity, and only partial local protections. Official 'radically pro-transgender' threat framing raises severity. Remedies exist but are partial, and custody harm remains unremedied. An adult alone faces mainly border/document and federal-facility exposure; an adult with a trans minor also faces care-ban and school-related hostility. This sits in the high-risk band.

entry_documents.exposure: National passport sex-marker restrictions; X markers halted for new issues; entry screening may refuse cases with document discrepancy or reasonable doubt about sex and consider lifetime fraud ineligibility; passports reported confiscated or blocked.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; fraud finding is not automatic and requires four elements; passport policy is challenged in court; legal-aid FAQ exists.
entry_documents.interaction: A foreign passport or visa encounter can move into refusal, secondary screening, or immigration detention; division adds no separate entry rule.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of transgender men; national corrections policies impose conversion-therapy-like measures and deny care.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity, but no documented custody remedy offsets the reported practices; corrections reporting on transgender prisoners stopped.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border document discrepancy or suspected misrepresentation can lead to immigration detention, where the documented custody harms apply.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National executive order bars transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with gender identity; many states/provinces ban such access. Division bans school facilities by birth sex but has no statewide adult rule.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division has no statewide adult bathroom ban; private hotels may be inclusive; 19 municipalities have local public-accommodations protections.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National facility exclusion reaches federal settings; division school rule affects students locally, not adult visitors generally.

care_services.exposure: Division bans puberty blockers and hormone therapy for minors with no phase-out; national orders frame gender-affirming care as mutilation and propose insurance bars; custody care denial reported.
care_services.protection: Adult emergency care is not documented as restricted; division bars conversion therapy on minors by executive order; care-ban litigation continues.
care_services.interaction: A trans minor travelling with an adult cannot access blocked care in the division; adult care access is less documented but national hostility affects institutions.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups among priorities; DOJ guidance uses 'radical gender ideology'; division hate-crime statute excludes gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 22 states/provinces plus capital district outlaw gender-identity discrimination; courts have blocked some orders.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat framing raises severity and may influence police response, while division bias enhancement is unavailable for anti-trans violence.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division restricts transgender students to birth-sex school facilities and bans minors' gender-affirming care; national orders direct investigations of schools and prosecution of teachers using preferred names or pronouns.
minors_guardians.protection: Care ban is under appeal; conversion therapy on minors is barred; no phase-out for existing patients is documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian travelling with a trans minor faces care-access barriers and school-related official hostility; adult-only travel avoids the school rule but not national care rhetoric.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No division trans-specific violence statistics are reported; division hate-crime statute omits gender identity; national official hostility may worsen reporting climate.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 19 municipal ordinances cover gender identity; no documented police sweeps or organized targeting in division.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse for anti-trans violence is uneven: national hate-crime coverage exists, but division bias enhancement does not, and local protections are municipal only.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport restrictions, entry-screening fraud exposure, care ban and custody harms remain operative or unresolved; religious-exemption statute can cut against local ordinances.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have enjoined some national orders; passport policy is litigated; national employment ruling protects transgender workers; legal aid and equality maps exist.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Relief is partial and depends on which measures are in force; custody practices are documented but not shown remedied.

anchor_checks.comparison: Like 0.35-A, this regime has an institutional facility exclusion and rejected or partial remedies, but the division lacks a statewide adult bathroom ban. It is worse on border/document screening and documented custody harm, so it sits near rather than clearly above 0.35.

0.45-A has a birth-sex public-building bathroom rule but no documented border or custody harm. This jurisdiction is lower because national entry screening, possible lifetime fraud ineligibility and severe immigration-custody reports add traveller-facing exposures beyond a facilities rule.

0.25-D combines universal birth-sex facilities, rejected complaints, police stops and extortion. This jurisdiction has no documented organized police sweeps or routine extortion in the division, so it is higher, though national custody harm and border screening keep it below reduced-risk anchors.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is a patchwork: no general criminalisation and no division-wide adult bathroom ban, but national document and border rules create outing and refusal risk, federal facilities exclude by birth sex, and immigration/corrections custody carries documented severe harm. Division-level school-facility and minors' care restrictions affect families, while hate-crime and nondiscrimination protection is partial. Adults travelling alone face mainly entry/document and federal-facility exposure; adults with a trans minor face added care and school hostility. The result is high risk, not severe organised targeting, and not reduced risk.
